description:
Opts one text-bearing column on a SearchIndex in to AOSS Automatic Semantic Enrichment. At index-build time the matching column's field mapping is emitted with a semantic_enrichment block (status: ENABLED, language_options derived from languageMode); AOSS then auto-attaches its managed sparse model to the ingest path and rewrites match queries (standalone or inside bool / boosting / constant_score / dis_max / function_score / hybrid compound queries) against this field into neural sparse queries. multi_match queries are not rewritten by AOSS.

Per-column opt-in is the only path to semantic enrichment — there is no SearchConfiguration-level default for the same reason there is no default analyzer: AOSS meters indexing-inference TPS against the collection (soft cap of 100 TPS per the AWS docs) and bills OpenSearch Compute Units (OCUs) for the sparse-model work, so vectorizing every text column by default would inflate spend on every indexed row.

Which columns are eligible: top-level text-typed Synapse columns (STRING, MEDIUMTEXT, LARGETEXT, LINK). The AWS docs limit AOSS Automatic Semantic Enrichment to top-level text fields, so STRING_LIST / nested-style columns are silently skipped at index-build time with a warning in SearchIndexStatus.errorMessage, mirroring how ColumnAnalyzerOverrideEntry handles missing columns.

Example:

{ "columnName": "abstract", "languageMode": "MULTI_LINGUAL" }

columnName.description: The name of the column to enrich. Must match a top-level text-typed column in the SearchIndex's resolved schema. Silently skipped at index-build time if the column is not present or is not text-typed — a single SearchConfiguration can therefore apply to several SearchIndexes that share some column names.

languageMode.description: The language mode AOSS should use for this column. Defaults to ENGLISH if omitted.
